newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico govt to take stake in highways -- ICA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico govt to take stake in highways -- ICA.

text.p: The Mexican government is likely to take an equity stake in the private highways it originally had built under private concessions as part of a rescue plan to bail out the loss-making projects, an official from the construction company ICA told Reuters.
"It is almost certain that (the government) will come in as a shareholder," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
During the 1988-94 administration of President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, the government handed out concessions for 52 highways totalling 5,683 km as well as eight bridges.
Most of the projects charge extremely high tolls and as a result are almost empty of traffic and incapable of repaying their debts.
President Ernesto Zedillo, in his annual report to Congress at the start of September, said the federal government would provide 14 billion pesos in support to rescue the projects.
"The government will take the bank debt and convert it into capital. There will be a swap of debt for capital," the source said.
